root_cause: The EasyOCR 'detector' model conversion/inference subprocess crashed on the Windows NPU runner with exit code 3221225477 (0xC0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION). This is not tied to the PR under test (#38209 only touches a GPU FP16 precision transformation for Qwen-Image gated residual, unrelated to EasyOCR/NPU model-hub conversion). The multiprocessing wrapper (multiprocessing_utils.py) detected the child process exited via an OS-level access violation rather than a Python exception, consistent with a native crash inside the NPU driver/runtime or model conversion path for this specific model, not a deterministic code regression from the PR diff.
reproduction_steps: Run pytest install/tests/model_hub_tests/pytorch/test_easyocr.py::TestEasyOCRConvertModel::test_convert_model -k 'NPU-detector' on a Windows machine with an NPU device and the same driver/runtime stack as the CI runner (5020 platform). Reproduction outside CI is unreliable since it depends on native NPU driver state.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed NPU Models Tests job; access-violation crashes in native NPU inference are frequently transient runner/driver state issues.

If the failure recurs consistently for the EasyOCR detector model, escalate to the NPU plugin team to check for a native crash (e.g., via crash dump or driver logs) in the detector model's compiled graph.
Consider adding a skip/xfail marker for this specific model on NPU precommit until root-caused, if it keeps blocking unrelated merge-queue PRs.
prevention_strategies: Track NPU model-hub test stability separately from PR-specific validation; consider adding a health-check gate that flags known-flaky NPU model tests instead of blocking the merge queue for unrelated changes.
historical_context: No prior pattern record for this specific ProcessError/signal combination was found in the CI Doctor MQ database. A related but distinct pattern (EasyOCR model download failing with HTTP 504) has occurred twice (signature_hash 9cb03e077ef3024a), confirming EasyOCR-related NPU/PyTorch model-hub tests have a history of infrastructure-level flakiness in this repository.
